name: Gfx_Sprite2D_UpdateTouchAndIsBusy
summary: Advances the object's touch state machine one step and reports whether the touch sequence is still running: it returns 0 only once the phase byte has reached its terminal value 5 (release sent).
evidence: NEW: func_0064C740 is disassembled at 0x0064C740 as `ldrb r0,[r0]; cmp r0,#5; moveq r0,#1; movne r0,#0; bx lr` - a pure 'phase == 5' getter, not an unknown helper. Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState writes phase 5 as the terminal state after sending the release, so `!(phase == 5)` means 'still in the touch sequence'. The old name claimed the inverse ('IsReady') and a 'handle' argument; the argument is the object itself (r0 is forwarded unchanged to both callees). Class prefix from the code region (Gfx_Sprite2D_DeletingDtorA/CreateMeshA/DtorB/CreateMeshB) and from the sibling getter 0x001A3C80, vtable slot 0x00759040, which returns self+0x4D8.

name: Actor2D_UpdateTouchAndIsBusy
summary: Advances the 2D actor's touch state machine one step and reports whether the touch sequence is still running (0 only at the terminal phase 5).
evidence: NEW: byte-identical to 0x001A3C88 and now fully explained - Field_Object2D_UpdateTouchState(self) then func_0064C740(self), which the disassembly at 0x0064C740 shows is `*(u8*)self == 5`. The class is Actor2D: the function sits in the Actor2D_* code region and its sibling getter 0x0021B508 is vtable slot 0x0075BE14 of the Actor2D vtable (0x0075BE10 = 0x0021B6F0 Actor2D_RefreshTouchInfo). The old name 'TestStateAfterScroll' described neither the update nor the polarity.

name: Actor2D_SpriteNode_UpdateTouchAndIsBusy
summary: Advances the 2D actor sprite node's touch state machine one step and reports whether the touch sequence is still running (0 only at the terminal phase 5).
evidence: NEW: same 28-byte body as 0x001A3C88/0x0021B510/0x003A1CD0, now explained by the disassembly of func_0064C740 (`*(u8*)self == 5`). The class is Actor2D_SpriteNode, not a generic 'Gfx sprite': the sibling getter 0x00290578 is vtable slot 0x0075D908, inside the vtable 0x0075D888 installed by Actor2D_SpriteNode_Ctor (0x002907D8). The old name 'IsSpriteHidden' had the wrong polarity and no class evidence.

name: Field_Gadget_UpdateTouchAndIsBusy
summary: Advances the field gadget's touch state machine one step and reports whether the touch sequence is still running (0 only at the terminal phase 5).
evidence: NEW: same 28-byte body as the other three copies, now explained by the disassembly of func_0064C740 (`*(u8*)self == 5`). The class is Field_Gadget: the function sits between Field_Gadget_CreateSprite (0x003A1C28) and Gfx_SpriteActor_InitEightQuads (0x003A1CEC), and its sibling getter 0x003A1CC8 is vtable slot 0x007677DC, immediately after the Field_Gadget touch-record slot 0x007677D8 (0x003A1EB0). The old name 'IsTouchOutside' described a hit test that is not in the body.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_RefreshTouchInfoB
summary: Rebuilds the sprite's secondary touch record (kind 0x0A) from its position and mesh id and caches the six fields at self+0x3B8..+0x3C0; it first drops stale objects of the touch class through Ui_DestroyObjectsOfClass.
evidence: NEW: the body is the same template as 0x001A3E68 with kind 0x0A and destination +0x3B8, and the leading call is now named - Ui_DestroyObjectsOfClass (0x004DD70C) destroys every live object of the touch class before the record is rebuilt, which is why the function is not a plain getter. It is not a vtable slot (no reference in asm/rodata), so the 'B' suffix stays as the only way to tell it from 0x001A3E68.

name: Gfx_Sprite2D_RefreshTouchInfo
summary: Rebuilds the sprite's touch record (kind 2) from its position and mesh id and caches the six fields at self+0x4D8..+0x4E0; returns 1.
evidence: NEW: this is vtable slot 0x0075903C of the Gfx_Sprite2D vtable, and the very next slot 0x00759040 is 0x001A3C80, which returns self+0x4D8 - i.e. the refresh slot is immediately followed by the getter for the record it fills. That slot pairing (refresh, then get) is repeated in five sibling classes (0x0075A038/0x0075A03C, 0x0075BE10/0x0075BE14, 0x0075D904/0x0075D908, 0x007677D8/0x007677DC), so 'refresh the touch record' is confirmed rather than guessed.

name: Ui_Widget_RefreshTouchInfo
summary: Rebuilds a widget's touch record (kind 4) and copies it plus the resolved frame-table row fields into self+0x4D8..+0x4F4; returns 1.
evidence: NEW: vtable slot 0x0075A038, and the next slot 0x0075A03C is 0x001D6EA8, already named Ui_Widget_IsTouchActive - the getter for the same record. The refresh/get slot pair is the same one seen in the five sibling classes, so both the class (Ui_Widget) and the operation are confirmed.

name: Actor2D_RefreshTouchInfo
summary: Rebuilds the 2D actor's touch record (kind 7) from its position and mesh id and caches the six fields at self+0x4D8..+0x4E0; returns 1.
evidence: NEW: vtable slot 0x0075BE10, immediately followed by slot 0x0075BE14 = 0x0021B508, the getter that returns self+0x4D8. The refresh/get slot pair matches the five sibling classes, so the operation and the Actor2D class are confirmed.

name: Actor2D_SpriteNode_RefreshTouchInfo
summary: Rebuilds the 2D actor sprite node's touch record (kind 3) from its position and mesh id and caches the six fields at self+0x4D8..+0x4E0; returns 1.

name: Ui_Shop_EnsureGold
signature: int Ui_Shop_EnsureGold(void* record, int arg2, int arg3, int context)
summary: Shop-close guard: reads the gold counter (bag slot 10 = bag+0x28) and, when it is below the shop record's +0x18 amount, writes that amount back, so the player never leaves the shop with less gold than the record expects.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly at 0x001C0EBC..0x001C0F00 shows the dropped third argument - `ldr r2,[r5,#0x18]` loads record+0x18, `cmp r2,r0` compares it with the value read by func_0066B0F8(bag,10), and the conditional `bl 0x612B08` still has r2 = record+0x18, so the write is `bag[10] = record->f_18`. func_00612B08 is `*(u32*)(bag + idx*4 + 0x2998) = value`, and idx 10 * 4 = 0x28, which is exactly the gold slot from FACTS.md. The only caller is the confident Ui_ShopWindow_Dtor.

name: Ui_Window_AppendControlBytes
summary: Window script-command handler: takes the command's parameter from the source record at self+0x11E4 (+0xA4), clamps it, stores it at self+0x1114 and appends the control bytes 0x09 followed by 0x11 (clamped) or 0x12 (not clamped) to the window's byte vector at self+0x10A8.

The body appends two bytes (0x09 then 0x11 or 0x12) through Container_InlineVector8B_PushByte, so the old 'AppendByte' singular was slightly off; it is not item code (no Item_LookupRecord, no member inventory).

name: Ui_Window_ProjectWorldSlot

name: Ui_Overlay_UpdateBillboard
summary: Projects a UI overlay anchor into screen space: adds the animated offset at +0x6E0..+0x6E8 to the local offset, projects it, writes the quad position at self->f_30 (+0x1C/+0x20/+0x24 and the +0x44 flag), then applies a per-slot parallax offset for slots 0 and 1.

name: maybe_Svc_IsFeatureAvailable
summary: Two-step availability gate: returns 1 only when both IPC queries succeed. The two callees are the CTR IPC wrappers for command ids 0x08170000 and 0x08180000, each of which returns one response byte; which service or feature they query is still unknown.
evidence: NEW: the two bodyless callees are now identified - 0x00503F58 calls Svc_Ipc_Send08170000 (0x00505AB0) and 0x00503F8C calls Svc_Ipc_Send08180000 (0x00505AE8), both of which build the request in TLS+0x80, issue `svc 0x32` (svcSendSyncRequest) and return the response byte. So the shape 'both queries must succeed' is confirmed, but the command ids 0x0817/0x0818 are not mapped to a named 3DS service, so the feature name stays unknown and the maybe_ stays.

name: Gfx_ApplyScreenViewFades
summary: Applies the parameter block's fade settings to the screen views it names: for each of the four view ids at params+0x48 (0x0FFFFFFF = end) it resolves the view in the current screen block and calls Gfx_ScreenView_ApplyFadeParams on both view objects (+0x54 and +0xB10), skipping views whose +0x16D byte is set.
evidence: NEW: both callers are now named - Camera_UpdateViewTransition (0x004C82BC, 0.50) and Ui_SceneFlow_Update (0x0019E45C) - and the per-view action is the confident Gfx_ScreenView_ApplyFadeParams (0x00622674), applied to both screen-view blocks. So 'apply the fade parameters' is confirmed and the old 'select view' reading is gone.

name: Gfx_UpdateScreenViewTargets
summary: Resolves the parameter block's four view ids against the current screen block and, for each view that passes the +0x16D test, updates its camera target list through maybe_Camera_UpdateTargetList; returns 1 when at least one view was updated.
evidence: NEW: the caller is the confident Camera_UpdateViewTransition (0x004C82BC, 0.50) and the per-view action is maybe_Camera_UpdateTargetList (0x001D43C0), so this is the target half of the same camera-transition step whose fade half is 0x001D2DCC. The loop and the +0x16D skip test are identical in both, which confirms the pairing.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_HideCurrentChild
summary: Hides the window's current child subtree unless it is the embedded pane at self+0x168: it asks 0x001D86CC for the current child and, when that is neither null nor the built-in pane, broadcasts visibility flag 0 to it.
evidence: NEW: the disassembly at 0x001EABD8..0x001EAC00 shows the readable C's 64-bit split is a Ghidra artifact - the real body is `child = func_001D86CC(); if (child && child != self+0x168) Ui_Object_BroadcastToChildren(child, 0)`. Nothing is detached or freed, so the old 'DetachChild' wording was wrong; it only sets the hide flag. The class is still only supported by the caller Ui_ActivateScreenMessageAndModel (0x00311530), so the maybe_ stays.

name: maybe_Ui_Window_ResetChildrenA
summary: Window reset step: flushes the pending callbacks (0x00316410), drains the child ring to zero, re-links the two embedded panes at +0x3E0 and +0x4A4 and broadcasts visibility flag 1 to the first.
evidence: NEW: the shared callees are now identified from the disassembly, and none of them frees anything - func_0062F070 (0x0062F070) counts the children of the intrusive ring at self+0x110, func_0010EBD8 (0x0010EBD8) detaches one child from that ring and re-initialises its node, func_00123594 (0x00123594) splices an embedded pane node back into the ring, and Ui_Object_BroadcastToChildren (0x001A5F9C) only calls virtual +0x1C on each child. So the old 'DestroyChildren' wording was wrong: the function resets the ring to the class's fixed set of embedded panes and then sets their visibility.
